basis.governing_question: How can Metalúrgica Norte cut conversion cost across its six plants in Portugal and Spain and put the improvements in place in every plant?

sub_questions.question: What is conversion cost per part in each plant today, and where does it arise?
Which opportunities cut conversion cost per part most, and how large is each plant's potential?
Which changes show a measurable drop in conversion cost per part at the pilot plant?
How do the proven changes get running in the remaining five plants?
How is the cost-per-part reduction tracked against the baseline in every plant?

drivers.evidence: six plants in Portugal and Spain

work.unit: Site diagnosed on the floor (cost baseline, line observation, loss analysis)

phase_work.why: Three of six plants diagnosed, two at once, the rest extended from data; above typical 3-6 weeks because the sample needs two rounds.

work.unit: Pilot site: changes made and savings shown in the cost data
Rollout wave of up to 3 sites

phase_work.why: Pilot plant first, then five plants in two waves of up to three; above typical 8-16 weeks because the work adds up.

sizing.levers: Running the two rollout waves side by side would save 4 to 6 weeks; diagnosing two plants instead of three saves 2 to 3.

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Baseline conversion cost per part at three representative plants and size the improvement opportunities across all six.

gate.label: Initiatives go/no-go
gate.decision: Go or no-go on implementing the sized initiatives, starting at the pilot plant?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Show the cost saving at a pilot plant, then roll the changes out to the other five plants.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the final results and the handover of the initiatives to the plant teams?

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given, so 25 to 29 weeks is an estimate; confirm the length before this becomes a quote.
Implementation takes the middle of a 16 to 24 week estimate and reaches the top if the pilot needs 12 weeks, each wave 6.
Plan assumes one pilot plant among the six, then two waves of up to three plants each; confirm the sequence.
Diagnosis covers three representative plants and extends to the other three from data; confirm the sample and which plants.
No Measurement phase: confirm whether tracking cost per part after the last wave is in scope or ends with Implementation.
